Would You Make Your BMW X6 M Look Like This?
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozport
Unlike its more practical (and better looking, this writer thinks) sibling, the X5, which has been replaced by a new generation , the BMW X6 is here to stay, for now anyway, because its replacement is reportedly due some two years from now, probably debuting in late 2028, and hitting dealers nationwide for the 2029 model year.
By then, the current third-gen will be more than nine years old, as the assembly commenced back in August 2019. The G06 is based on the CLAR platform, just like the older X5, the previous 7 Series, 8 Series, first-gen X7, and the controversial XM. Its successor, on the other hand, will build on an updated version of the same construction. How do we know that? Because so does the new-age X5, and the future X6 will follow in its footsteps.
Besides the architecture, we also know what it will look like, even if BMW is pretty much delaying the inevitable, because it will step into the Neue Klasse era. This means a vizor-like face similar, or perhaps identical, to that of the new BMW X5 , albeit with a sloping roofline, less space in the trunk, and less headroom for backseat occupants. The cockpit will also be identical, so if you want to see what the interior of the future X6 will look like, then look at the X5’s. Or the 3er, i3, iX3, and so on.
With this information off our chest, let’s move on to the pictured BMW X6 M, which is the real reason behind this story. Images of it were shared on social media by RevoZport earlier this week, with the tuner stating that the vehicle in question wears its “street kit.” And if that sounds familiar, then you have likely seen our coverage of the F95 BMW X5 M , which is also equipped with the tuner’s “street kit.”
Photo: Instagram | revozport Just like its more practical sibling, this BMW X6 M features the same goodies, more or less. The less part includes the hood, which hasn’t been changed. The apron, on the other hand, is new, and so is the kidney grille surround, from what we can tell. Further back, the premium mid-size super crossover coupe, or the SAV (Sports Activity Vehicle), as BMW likes to call it, features new side skirt attachments, and the door mirror casings carry over from the factory.
At the rear, the BMW X6 M in question has a much more pronounced ducktail spoiler. The multi-fin diffuser is part of the makeover, and the extras have been crafted from carbon fiber. The car has a gray look on the outside, rides on familiar wheels, and the add-ons have a forged carbon look that may sound like a bit too much, though it is not that flashy in reality, and we reckon other tuners (ahem, Mansory!) could learn a thing or two from RevoZport when it comes to this part, and not only.
The tinted windows, including the windshield, which features UV protection from what we can see, prevent us from catching a glimpse of the interior. Thus, we can assume that the upholstery and trim carry over from the factory, and this likely applies to the seats, steering wheel, door sills, and so on. What we are saying is that the cabin likely remains bone stock, and it’s up to you to decide whether that is a good or a bad thing.
Photo: Instagram | revozport We cannot end this story without mentioning the powertrain, and as you likely know, the F96-generation of the BMW X6 M features the company’s familiar V8 engine. It is a twin-turbocharged lump, which produces the exact same output and thrust as the one powering the F95 BMW X5 M. This means 617 brake horsepower, which translates to 625 metric horsepower and 460 kilowatts, with the peak output available at 6,000 rpm.
As for the thrust, it is available between 1,800 rpm and 4,600 rpm, and it is officially rated at 553 pound-feet (750 Nm) of torque. The BMW X6 M features a rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system, and an eight-speed automatic transmission channeling the power to both axles. It also has mild-hybrid assistance, and takes only 3.9 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill. That’s identical to the era’s X5 M, and one-tenth of a second faster than the pre-facelifted iteration.
A brand new BMW X6 M will set you back a minimum of $136,100 in the United States of America for the latest model year. That is the official MSRP as the brand’s website reveals, and it obviously excludes destination, as well as options, and dealer fees. The old BMW X5 M is still listed on the website, and it is accompanied by an MSRP of $131,000.
Now, if you owned a BMW X6 M and came across RevoZport’s pictured tuning package, would you say yes or no to it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by RevoZport (@revozportt)
